Scientists discover a bizarre Jurassic “squid” unlike anything ever seen
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-20
12:20:44 UTC
21:20:44 KST

Scientists discover a bizarre Jurassic “squid” unlike anything ever seen
- Date:
- October 20, 2026
- Source:
- University of Manchester
- Summary:
- Scientists have identified the “fattest” belemnite ever discovered, a bizarre, barrel-shaped squid relative that lived in Wyoming’s ancient seas 160 million years ago. The exceptionally rare fossils reveal a creature unlike anything previously known, potentially a predator of smaller squid-like animals and a surprising survivor of a supposedly vanished family.
- Share:
Two extraordinarily rare fossils found in Wyoming have revealed a strange new species of squid relative that lived approximately 160 million years ago, during the Jurassic Period.
Named Wyoteuthis linsterorum, the prehistoric creature belonged to an extinct group of marine animals known as belemnites, which were related to modern squid and octopuses. What makes this species particularly remarkable is its unusually thick, barrel-shaped internal skeleton, earning it the distinction of being the "chunkiest" or "fattest" belemnite ever identified.
An international research team from the United States, United Kingdom, and New Zealand, including Dr. Dean Lomax, an Honorary Research Fellow at The University of Manchester, detailed the discovery in the scientific journal Papers in Palaeontology.
An Unusually Thick Jurassic Squid Relative
Belemnites are among the most frequently discovered fossils in the world. They are best known for their distinctive, bullet-shaped internal skeletal structures, called rostra or guards, which are often the only parts of the animals that survive in the fossil record.
Wyoming's Sundance Formation, which preserves evidence of an ancient inland sea that once stretched across much of the western United States, has yielded millions of these fossils. According to Wyoming paleontologist and study coauthor Jessica Lippincott, they are commonly nicknamed "squid butts" in the region.
Most belemnite fossils from Wyoming have a narrow, bullet-shaped appearance, typically measuring between 5 and 10 centimeters in length and just 1 to 2 centimeters across. The newly identified species is dramatically different. Its rostrum measures approximately 10 centimeters long but reaches an extraordinary 6 centimeters in width, making it the thickest known example of its kind.
Scientists estimate that the living animal, including its arms, could have reached a total length of approximately 60 centimeters, or about two feet.
Rare Fossils Reveal a Surprising Evolutionary Secret
Wyoming paleontologist Bill Wahl, who has devoted much of his career to searching for fossils across the state, recognized that the unusual specimen deserved closer examination. He said the belemnite "stuck out like a sore thumb" compared with the countless others found in the region.
Wahl assembled an international team to investigate the fossils, bringing in specialists including belemnite expert Alexey Ippolitov, a PhD student now based at Victoria University of Wellington in New Zealand.
The researchers used computed tomography (CT) scanning to investigate the fossils' internal structures without damaging the specimens. These detailed scans revealed an unexpected connection to an ancient belemnite family that scientists had believed disappeared millions of years before this animal lived.
Ippolitov said he was "deeply surprised" to encounter such an unusual specimen from a group that has already been studied extensively. Belemnites have been the subject of paleontological research for more than 200 years, making the identification of such a radically different species especially remarkable.
The creature's unusual proportions may also offer clues about how it lived and hunted.
Ippolitov explains: "A possible explanation is that their relatively large size gave them an advantage when hunting co-occurring smaller belemnites of the genus Pachyteuthis. Modern squid, after all, are hardly picky when it comes to prey: they readily hunt not only other species of cephalopods, but sometimes even their own kind."
A Fossil Discovery Nearly 30 Years in the Making
Although the species has only now been formally described, its discovery began almost three decades ago.
The first known specimen was found in the late 1990s by Dr. Burkhard Pohl, founder of the Wyoming Dinosaur Center. While examining fossils, Pohl noticed a belemnite that was considerably larger than any he had previously encountered.
Despite its unusual appearance, the specimen remained unstudied in a museum collection drawer for many years.
A breakthrough came when fossil collector Cliff Linster discovered a second specimen near Ten Sleep, Wyoming. He donated the fossil to the Wyoming Dinosaur Center in 2019, providing researchers with another example of the mysterious animal.
With two specimens available for comparison, scientists finally had enough evidence to recognize and formally describe an entirely new species.
The genus name Wyoteuthis means "a squid from Wyoming," while the species name linsterorum recognizes Cliff Linster and his family for their contributions. Linster discovered one of the only two known examples and ensured it was available for scientific research.
Lippincott emphasized how extraordinary the discovery was, even for researchers familiar with Wyoming's abundant belemnite fossils.
"After spending years fossil hunting in Wyoming and collecting countless fossils of the common Pachyteuthis belemnites here in Wyoming, this one is unlike anything I have ever seen! It goes to show that we are still finding new species of fossils all the time, and people who rockhound or collect invertebrate fossils can also contribute to science."
Honoring a Fossil Hunter's Remarkable Legacy
Sadly, Cliff Linster passed away in June before the research was published. He had been aware that scientists were investigating his discovery and was enthusiastic about seeing the unusual fossil receive formal scientific recognition.
The Linster family already had an impressive history of fossil discoveries, including their association with the famous dinosaur Bambiraptor.
For British paleontologist Dr. Dean Lomax, the discovery also carries considerable personal meaning. Lomax, an Honorary Research Fellow at The University of Manchester and an 1851 Research Fellow at the University of Bristol, first worked alongside Cliff and his wife, Sandy, while excavating dinosaur fossils as a teenager.
He said: "I met Cliff and Sandy in 2009, when I spent a week digging up a dinosaur bonebed on their property in northern Montana. I have fond memories of that dig, listening to Cliff share his passion for fossils, including this belemnite. I'm honored to help name this fossil after Cliff. It's bittersweet that he didn't get to see it published, but it's wonderful that we can immortalize him and his family name in the history of paleontology. The find is incredibly rare, which might be due to some ecological adaptations to the environment at the time. Perhaps its rarity is a result of narrow specialization."
Lomax has extensive experience studying Wyoming's prehistoric animals, including collecting fossils and excavating plesiosaurs and ichthyosaurs from the Sundance Formation. He is also the author of the recently published book "The Secret Lives of Dinosaurs," which features fossils from Wyoming.
The discovery highlights how even well-studied fossil groups can still hold major surprises, particularly when unusual specimens are preserved and made available for scientific investigation.
Both known fossils of Wyoteuthis linsterorum are now on display at the Wyoming Dinosaur Center in Thermopolis, Wyoming, where visitors can see the extraordinary remains of one of the Jurassic seas' most unusual squid relatives.
The findings are published in the international journal Papers in Palaeontology.

Expanding the Military Footprint: China’s New Air Base in Laos
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-20
12:17:00 UTC
21:17:00 KST

As China’s power and self-confidence grows, it’s becoming much more active in projecting that power by establishing military bases abroad. The latest is at Ban Keun Airport near Vientiane, where China has established a joint support and training facility with Laos, according to a September announcement by the Ministry of National Defense in Beijing.
It is the first overseas military facility that China has openly acknowledged, unlike the ones in Djibouti and Cambodia. This has several implications for the region.
But first, the base itself. Satellite imagery procured and analyzed by CNN shows a 2,000-meter-long runway, taxiway, and parking apron for 22 aircraft. CNN also reports rapid construction at the site. Other media reports mention that satellite photos show eight aircraft, likely Chinese-Pakistani Hongdu JL-8 training and light attack jets (also called K-8s), and more than two dozen support vehicles. Laos is known to own this type of aircraft, but fewer than the eight seen at the facility. Laos could have bought more, or the extras may be Chinese.
China has said that the facility is strictly for training Lao air force pilots, “enhancing practical military cooperation,” and “promoting regional peace and stability.” This sounds reasonable enough, but it conflicts with China’s own previous positions on foreign military facilities. It has been a vocal critic of the global U.S. military presence.
Establishment of the Laotian base follows a pattern in China’s growing external military presence and access. China established its first overseas military facility in Djibouti in 2017, maintaining then and now that it is merely a logistical facility. This is still its most distant foreign military base, sitting astride the crucial waters overlooking the Bab al-Mandab strait leading to the Red Sea.
Closer to home, a Washington Post story in 2022 revealed that China was upgrading the Cambodian Ream Naval Base, with the Chinese military being given “exclusive use” of parts of it. China and Cambodia initially denied the report, but last year they formally inaugurated the facility. Soon warships from both countries visited it, conducting joint military drills. Though the base is not very far from China’s own territory, it’s on the strategically crucial Gulf of Thailand and thereby strengthens China’s position in the Indo-Pacific and particularly in the South China Sea.
With the Ream Naval Base in Cambodia and Ban Keun Air Facility in Laos, China now has both naval and aviation logistics hubs in the area.
There are at least four implications from the establishment of the base in Laos, both for neighbors such as Vietnam and the whole region.
First, sitting to the west of Vietnam, it gives China one more pressure point on that country. Vietnam already has a complicated relationship with China, with close economic ties but also significant territorial disputes.
Second, it adds an air power dimension to China’s foreign base activity. The two foreign bases that China previously built were both naval ones. The latest base at Ban Keun provides China’s air force with an air power footing in a strategically sensitive region. China can be expected to later extend the runway to support Chinese surveillance aircraft or bombers. Though Laos is land-locked, its long and narrow geography could provide China with an excellent site for monitoring activity across Southeast Asia.
Third, this represents a new type of military basing activity. For China, what matters is assured access. By packaging access as joint training facilities or disaster relief and humanitarian support hubs, Beijing secures a more lasting presence while avoiding the diplomatic and political cost of building traditional military bases. As far as China is concerned, it has created pretty much the same strategic effect without investing in a dedicated Western-style base of its own. Also unlike Western bases, China’s decision to act on Ban Keun, as ASPI senior analyst Rachel Vandenbrink told Reuters, was “more about a target of opportunity than filling an obvious operational need.”
Finally, the ratcheting up of military pressure increasingly strains Southeast Asia’s traditional strategy of hedging, in which countries of the region integrate with China’s manufacturing strength while balancing it with U.S. military power. Regional powers will need to consider how long they can hedge when Chinese military power looms ever larger over them.
This article was originally published in ASPI’s The Strategist.

Ukrainian drone unit hit U.S. tank brigade hard in drills
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-20
12:16:54 UTC
21:16:54 KST

- Ukrainian drone operators caused about 70% of a U.S. Army armored brigade’s casualties in the first three days of an exercise in Germany.
- The brigade cut drone-caused losses below 30% by day three and later used over 700 drones to breach enemy lines.
Ukrainian drone operators playing the enemy in a U.S. Army training exercise in Germany caused about 70% of an American armored brigade’s casualties in the first three days, according to an account by the brigade’s own commander and staff.
The figures come from an article in Military Review, the U.S. Army’s professional journal, written by Col. Michael Ziegelhofer, commander of the 3rd Armored Brigade Combat Team, 1st Cavalry Division, known as “Greywolf,” and six of his officers. They describe Combined Resolve 26-07, held in spring 2026 at the Hohenfels Training Area in Bavaria, where the brigade fought an opposing force reinforced by a detachment from the 412th Regiment of Ukraine’s Unmanned Systems Forces, a unit known as “Nemesis.”
Enemy drones either struck Greywolf’s troops directly or spotted for artillery that did. Over the roughly 10-day rotation, the opposing force initiated contact with drones more than 750 times. By the end of the third day, the share of casualties caused by drones had fallen below 30%, and the authors say the enemy had not eased off. “Greywolf changed how it fought,” they wrote.
Much of that change came down to basic soldiering. The brigade’s counter-drone and electronic warfare systems jammed drone control signals in protective “bubbles” up to 2 km (1.2 miles) wide, but they had to be set up at fixed sites and moved forward in bounds, leaving units exposed on the move. The systems were also less effective against the smaller number of fiber-optic drones, which are guided through a thin cable and cannot be jammed. More than half the formation had to rely on cover, concealment, dispersion, smaller routes and fast battle drills to get away before artillery landed.
The authors estimate that roughly 60% of the counter-drone fight at brigade level is fieldcraft and drills. They said only the heavy simulated losses of the first days forced soldiers to apply what they had practiced. Survival came at a price: crews switched off Blue Force Tracker, cut radio use and even dropped Starshield satellite links to shrink their electronic signature, and resupplying the brigade took twice as long as planned because the enemy hunted its supply lines.
Greywolf also had drones of its own. For the offensive phase, it brought in the 3rd Battalion, 504th Parachute Infantry Regiment, then an experimental drone battalion, and employed more than 700 drones from platoon to brigade level. Using relay drones to extend their reach, nearly all of the battalion’s aircraft could fly 25 to 40 km (16 to 25 miles), enough to cover the entire training area, a box roughly 14 by 27 km.
That abundance initially swamped the brigade headquarters. Collection planning tools built for a handful of sensors broke down, the operations floor struggled to absorb the flood of reports, and an airspace system that opened and closed individual blocks for each drone could not keep up. The staff never had a complete picture of how many drones were in the air.
The brigade adapted by handing drone units clear priorities and letting them hunt within the commander’s intent instead of directing each aircraft. It moved its coordinated fire line forward of its cavalry squadron so drones and artillery could hit anything beyond it without extra clearance, made enemy drone ground control stations a top target, and held back part of its drone munitions for the decisive moment. Most crewed and uncrewed aircraft were separated by altitude, with narrow corridors reserved for attack helicopters and medical evacuation flights.
By the end of the rotation, Greywolf carried out two simultaneous breaches through dense forest about 6 km (3.7 miles) apart. The authors say the enemy could not tell which was the main effort, failed to stop either, and lost its reserve before committing it.
A company commander in the brigade, writing in Task & Purpose, described Nemesis drones already overhead as his company drove through the only gate into the training area.
“They showed us ways to effectively fly cheap drones incredible distances. They put on a masterclass in sensor-to-shooter kill chain management and speed using tactics, techniques, and technology that we can now use in our formations,” wrote Allan Watson.
The officers recommend that armored brigades house their drones in multifunctional strike troops, each with three platoons for long-range surveillance out to at least 40 km, medium and heavy bomber drones, and strike drones paired with relays, along with smaller armored strike platoons for each battalion. They also call for every drone in a brigade to share one common operational picture, pointing to Ukraine’s Delta battlefield management system as the model, and for counter-drone defenses that work on the move, from hard-kill protection on every vehicle up to brigade-level radar and defeat systems.
Ukrainian units and equipment have become a regular feature of U.S. Army training in Europe this year. Soldiers at Hohenfels were photographed during the following rotation, Combined Resolve 27-01, assembling a Ukrainian-designed Stork reconnaissance drone.

World Insights: Europe's housing crisis fuels social unrest
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-20
20:16:18 CST
21:16:18 KST

BRUSSELS, Oct. 20 (Xinhua) -- Protests have erupted in some European countries in recent weeks amid a housing crisis across Europe.
In Spain, demonstrators have pitched tents in central Madrid to protest soaring rents and evictions. Similar encampments have appeared in Portugal, where tens of thousands marched through Lisbon on Oct. 17, demanding relief from rising living costs and a deepening housing crisis. France, Italy and Belgium have also witnessed protests over a broader range of economic and social grievances.
While the protests have different causes, housing has emerged as a major source of discontent.
For Claudia, a young professional in Madrid, the Spanish capital, the problem is deeply personal. Despite holding two university degrees and working in the documentary industry, she still lives with her parents.
"It's simply impossible," she said when asked about living independently. Her father, she recalled, could rent a 70-square-meter apartment in Madrid for less than 100 euros a month when he was 18. For her generation, even education and employment offer no guarantee of similar independence.
Housing costs are a particular flashpoint in Spain and Portugal, but the squeeze is being felt across Europe.
A CRISIS BEYOND FOUR WALLS
In Budapest, finding a rental apartment can feel like a race against time. A woman searching for accommodation in the Hungarian capital told Xinhua that a property she had been interested in was rented out before she could even arrange a viewing.
Some landlords also impose strict requirements. "If you don't meet these requirements, you won't even get a chance to see the apartment," she said.
Between 2013 and 2024, house prices in nominal terms increased by more than 60 percent across the EU, growing faster than household income, with a number of member countries experiencing average increases of more than 220 percent, the Council of the EU said on Oct. 19. More than 1 million people across the bloc are estimated to be homeless.
Young people are particularly vulnerable. Eurostat data show that 26.9 percent of young people aged 15-29 in the EU lived in overcrowded households in 2025. The overcrowding rate for young people was 10.1 percentage points higher than for the total population.
In Spain, average monthly rent reached 1,176 euros (1,317 U.S. dollars), equivalent to 98.7 percent of the average monthly wage of a young person, according to the Spanish Youth Council.
The consequences have extended to education.
"We are facing the risk of a new form of social selection," Matthias Anbuhl, chair of the executive board of the German National Association for Student Affairs, said. "It is no longer simply talent and academic interest that determine which university someone can attend, but whether they can actually afford the rent in that city."
In France, only 45 percent of people aged 18 to 30 lived independently in 2025, according to the country's National Institute for Youth and Popular Education.
French economist Maxime Sbaihi pointed out that high housing costs and inadequate living space can discourage young adults from having children, potentially delaying parenthood and leading to smaller families.
Housing costs can also put better jobs out of reach. An International Monetary Fund study warned that declining housing affordability was restricting labor mobility and economic opportunity, making it harder for workers to move to areas offering better jobs.
SUPPLY LAGS BEHIND
For Edin, who works in Sarajevo, the capital of Bosnia and Herzegovina, homeownership has become an increasingly distant prospect. He said property prices in the city had almost doubled over the past four years.
Across Europe, housing supply has struggled to keep pace with demand, particularly in major cities.
Germany completed just 206,600 homes in 2025, down 18 percent from the previous year and the lowest number since 2012. The average time between building permits and completion rose from 20 months in 2020 to 27 months in 2025, according to Germany's Federal Statistical Office. The German Tenants' Association estimated a nationwide shortage of around 1.4 million homes.
Spain faces a similarly severe imbalance. Bank of Spain Deputy Governor Soledad Nunez estimated that the cumulative housing shortage since 2021 had reached approximately 755,000 units. She projected a further shortfall of about 300,000 units between 2026 and 2028.
Construction costs are one obstacle. In Poland, producer prices for new residential buildings rose 36 percent between 2021 and the third quarter of 2025, compared with an EU average of 24 percent, according to the European Commission.
Building permits are another obstacle. The Dutch government's coalition agreement says lengthy approval procedures and overlapping regulations mean new housing developments can take years to build.
Labor shortages and higher financing costs also make it harder to expand housing supply.
NO QUICK FIX
European governments are under pressure to make housing more affordable for renters and buyers alike. Many are searching for ways to offer relief now while tackling a shortage that has built up over years.
Increasing supply is central to the Dutch government's response. Its coalition agreement acknowledges that the Netherlands has repeatedly missed its target of building 100,000 homes a year and promises a stronger central government role in planning and construction.
Making better use of existing buildings offers another way to ease housing shortages. But many vacant properties are not fit to live in. More than half of vacant dwellings in Portugal, about 350,000 units, are thought to require medium-scale renovations to become inhabitable, according to the OECD.
For those at greatest risk, the immediate priority is keeping a roof overhead. A recommendation adopted by the Council of the EU on Oct. 19 called for emergency rental assistance and earlier intervention to prevent homelessness, alongside investment in new and renovated affordable housing.
For European governments facing public anger, the test is whether their policies bring an affordable home within reach. ■

Economic Watch: China's economy sustains growth as innovation, openness gain ground
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-20
20:16:17 CST
21:16:17 KST

BEIJING, Oct. 20 (Xinhua) -- Official data released Monday showed China's gross domestic product (GDP) grew 4.6 percent year on year in the first three quarters of this year, as the economy maintained steady growth under pressure and continued shifting toward new growth drivers.
International observers said China's resilience, innovation-driven development and continued opening up are helping it navigate external uncertainty while creating opportunities for the global economy.
SUSTAINING GROWTH AMID GLOBAL HEADWINDS
Conflicts in the Middle East, energy shocks, financial risks, tariff barriers and extreme weather have heightened global uncertainty. Yet China's economy continued to expand, with GDP rising 4.5 percent year on year in the third quarter, up from 4.3 percent in the second quarter.
According to data from China's National Bureau of Statistics, the economy added 5.7 trillion yuan (about 851.9 billion U.S. dollars) in output in the January-September period, the largest increase for the same period in five years. In September, value-added industrial output rose 5.5 percent year on year, the services production index increased 4.8 percent and retail sales grew 1.1 percent.
Rhys Roberts, national president and chair of the Australia China Business Council, told Xinhua that the figures demonstrated "the resilience of its (China's) economy amid global uncertainty."
"The figures provide grounds for confidence that China can achieve its full-year growth target of 4.5 to 5 percent," Roberts said.
China is less vulnerable than some countries with comparable debt levels, said Rodrigo Valdes, director of the International Monetary Fund's (IMF's) Fiscal Affairs Department.
"In particular, China has many assets, some of them liquid. The financial account, or the balance of payments, is not fully open, and that also cautions against big movements of capital," Valdes said.
China also pays relatively low interest rates compared with other countries and has a high savings rate, he said. "All these factors, I would say, help reduce the risks."
"Sustaining growth within the 4-to-5-percent range reflects the strength of China's economic foundations, the diversity of its industrial base, and its capacity to adapt to changing domestic and international conditions," said Jackson Kagobora, head of the Department of Economics at Kigali Independent University.
"China's experience demonstrates that resilience is not simply about withstanding external shocks, but also about continuously adapting, innovating and creating new opportunities for development," Kagobora added.
INNOVATING FOR GROWTH
From coffee-delivery drones and wireless phone charging at bus stops to wearable exoskeletons for Great Wall visitors, new technologies are making innovation in China visible in everyday life. High-end manufacturing, the digital economy and modern services are also emerging as key growth drivers.
"Structural optimization and dynamic transition represent the most prominent highlights at this stage," said Christine Susanna Tjhin, director of strategic communication and research at Indonesia's Gentala Institute.
"Modern services, the digital economy and high-end manufacturing have emerged as the primary growth engines ... these new growth drivers contributed over 40 percent to economic expansion in the first half of the year," she said, adding that the shift reflects progress in fostering new quality productive forces.
Simphiwe Madikizela, a professor at the University of South Africa's Graduate School of Business and Leadership, said the shift toward innovation-driven growth marks a structural change in China's development model.
"The focus is increasingly on improving productivity, technological capability and the value of goods and services produced, rather than depending exclusively on the expansion of conventional manufacturing capacity," Madikizela said.
Trade in industrial robots, electronic components, computer parts and electrical equipment exceeded 10 trillion yuan in the first three quarters, up 58.9 percent year on year and contributing 11.3 percentage points to overall trade growth, according to China's General Administration of Customs.
Integrated circuit exports surged 99.1 percent year on year during the period. Exports of electric vehicles, lithium batteries, and wind power generating sets and their parts rose 72.3 percent, 36.4 percent and 22.4 percent, respectively.
Michael Schumann, chairman of the board of the German Federal Association for Economic Development and Foreign Trade, said visits to China have given him a firsthand view of the country's industrial dynamism.
"The level of automation and production efficiency was truly impressive," Schumann said while recalling his tour at Xiaomi's electric-vehicle factory in Beijing. "China's dynamic innovation environment is like a 'fitness room' for foreign companies, allowing them to test their capabilities, adapt to new developments and strengthen their competitiveness."
EXPANDING GLOBAL LINKS
China's goods trade with 169 countries and regions rose 18.8 percent year on year to 39.94 trillion yuan in the first three quarters, with trade up 27.5 percent in September alone.
Since May 1, China has extended zero-tariff treatment to all 53 African countries with which it has diplomatic relations, bringing the total number of countries covered by its zero-tariff measures to 63. Imports from these countries reached 867.53 billion yuan in the first three quarters, up 15.3 percent year on year. China has been the world's second-largest import market for 17 consecutive years.
These figures "reflect China's extensive integration into the global economy and its importance as both a major supplier and a significant market for goods from around the world," said Kagobora, from Kigali Independent University.
China's "continued commitment to opening up, diversifying trade partnerships and facilitating market access contributes to international economic stability by supporting the movement of goods, sustaining production networks and creating opportunities for businesses across different regions," he added.
Thomas Helbling, deputy director of the IMF's Asia and Pacific Department, said China is making efforts to uphold a multilateral, rules-based trading system.
He said Chinese companies can play an important role in disseminating new technologies and supporting their application through outbound investment.
China's trade with countries under the Belt and Road cooperation reached 20.37 trillion yuan, up 17.1 percent year on year. Chinese companies have established more than 50,000 overseas enterprises, nearly 90 percent of them in countries of the Global South.
China's role in the Global South has been invaluable for economic development, said Lawrence Freeman, a U.S. political-economic analyst specializing in Africa with more than 30 years of experience in African economic development policy.
Freeman said the Belt and Road cooperation has helped attract much-needed infrastructure investment across the developing world, including power-generation facilities, railways, ports and airports in Africa.
"We must recognize that the future of the planet lies in the development of the Global South," Freeman said. ■

China Focus: China gains favor with foreign visitors as visa-free arrivals rise
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-20
20:16:13 CST
21:16:13 KST

BEIJING, Oct. 20 (Xinhua) -- China continued to attract more foreign visitors in the third quarter of 2026, with visa-free entries rising 24.1 percent year on year to nearly 9 million, official data showed Tuesday.
Foreign nationals made 23.27 million border crossings from July to September, up 15.6 percent year on year, according to the National Immigration Administration (NIA).
Visa-free entries accounted for 77.5 percent of all entries by foreign nationals during the period.
Overall, Chinese border authorities handled 192 million entries and exits during the quarter, a year-on-year increase of 7.9 percent.
From "China Travel" and "China Shopping" to "Chinamaxxing" and "China Haul," China-related trends have gained traction in recent years.
During China's week-long National Day holiday in early October, "China Haul" referred to videos in which foreign visitors arrive in China with empty suitcases, fill them with purchases and share videos of their hauls online.
The growing popularity of such trends comes amid China's efforts to facilitate inbound travel through expanded visa-free policies, improved infrastructure and more convenient services for international visitors.
Since December 2023, when China launched a trial policy granting unilateral visa exemptions to visitors from six countries, it has expanded unilateral visa-free entry to travelers from 50 countries as of September. The policy allows eligible visitors to stay for up to 30 days.
It also extended the visa-free transit period for certain countries from 72 or 144 hours to 240 hours in December 2024. There are 57 eligible countries so far.
As visitor numbers rise, tourist attractions across China are introducing AI-powered tourism assistants that offer real-time multilingual interactions, while mobile payment services are becoming more accessible to international visitors.
Some scenic areas have also set up international shipping service points, enabling overseas visitors to send their purchases directly to destinations around the world.
DIVERSE EXPERIENCES
For many visitors, the appeal of China extends beyond shopping and sightseeing at famous landmarks to exploring everyday life.
A Dutch tourist traveled to Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, on an independent trip this summer. Along with friends, the tourist visited local wet markets and parks, seeking a glimpse into everyday life in China.
"Many of the vegetables here aren't available in my hometown. It's fascinating," the visitor said.
Medical tourism is also emerging as another draw for international visitors. An international medical tourism pilot zone in Hainan Province has reported a sharp increase in overseas medical tourists this year, with visitors coming from nearly 20 countries and regions.
Tianjin Municipality has also introduced curated tourism routes centered on traditional Chinese medicine, combining sightseeing with cultural experiences, wellness services, product purchases and educational activities.
"More foreign visitors are venturing into urban neighborhoods and rural communities to experience everyday life in China," said Wu Guoping, an industry insider, adding that from the nighttime economy in cities to rural revitalization, these experiences are giving visitors a more diverse and vivid picture of China.
China's 2026-2030 tourism development plan, released in July, proposes attracting 190 million inbound tourist visits a year by 2030, with annual inbound tourism spending exceeding 150 billion U.S. dollars.
The plan calls for developing specialized tourism products tailored to visitors from different countries and regions, featuring local cuisine, traditional crafts, history and culture, and technological experiences. It also encourages distinctive travel routes that blend traditional culture with modern experiences. ■

News Analysis: How new growth drivers are reshaping China's economy
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-20
20:16:02 CST
21:16:02 KST

BEIJING, Oct. 20 (Xinhua) -- China's new growth drivers are gaining strength as traditional sectors move up the value chain and emerging industries expand, according to officials and economists assessing the country's latest economic data.
China's gross domestic product grew 4.6 percent year-on-year in January-September, with third-quarter growth rising to 4.5 percent from 4.3 percent in the second quarter, data from the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) showed Monday.
Wei Qijia, a researcher at the State Information Center under the National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC), said China's economy showed upward momentum, stronger new growth drivers and an improving structure in the first nine months of 2026.
He noted China achieved relatively fast growth among major economies, advances in emerging industries and improvements in energy structure and export mix.
The NBS estimated that new drivers, including high-end manufacturing, the digital and intelligent economy and modern services, contributed more than 40 percent to economic growth in the first nine months. A further NBS analysis released Tuesday showed that new industrial drivers generated over 60 percent of industrial growth in the third quarter.
High-tech manufacturing value added increased 14.3 percent in the first nine months, compared with 5.3 percent for major industrial enterprises overall. NBS deputy head Mao Shengyong said the growth "baton" was being passed further toward new drivers, while traditional industries were also upgrading through new technology.
Mao cited ceramics makers in Jingdezhen using 3D printing to modernize production, as well as a coal enterprise where intelligent monitoring had boosted production efficiency by 30 percent. The NBS said such changes were helping established industries move toward higher-value production.
Industrial robots had been applied in 71 major industry categories of the national economy, with applications extending from welding and materials handling to precision assembly and quality checks, NBS data showed in June.
Liu Zhibiao, an industrial economist at Nanjing University, said that industrial clusters and supporting supply chains built up over decades had enabled several manufacturing sectors to grow faster.
The shift toward more technology-intensive production is reflected in investment. Investment in intellectual property products rose 9.3 percent in the first nine months, despite a decline in overall fixed-asset investment.
"Investment is undergoing a profound shift in emphasis from traditional sectors to emerging ones, and from scale expansion to efficiency improvement," said Liu Yuanchun, president of Shanghai University of Finance and Economics.
China's policy agenda has increasingly focused on this transition between old and new industries. The Central Economic Work Conference in December 2025 called for stepping up efforts to cultivate new growth drivers. A meeting of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee in July this year called for accelerating the shift from old to new growth drivers.
The shift comes as competition in advanced technologies intensifies globally and China seeks to match stronger production capabilities with new demand at home. Guidelines issued by the CPC Central Committee and the State Council this month call for upgrading traditional industries while developing emerging and future sectors, following the approach of "establishing the new before abolishing the old."
The NDRC has said this means ensuring that new productive capacity is firmly in place before outdated capacity is phased out in an orderly manner, allowing industrial chains and employment to adjust smoothly.
Zhu Qigui, professor at Shanghai Jiao Tong University, said China's economic fundamentals remained solid in the first nine months despite pressures, while new quality productive forces, modern services and high-tech trade continued to provide fresh growth momentum.
He attributed this resilience and vitality to four foundations: a complete industrial system and vast market, accumulated knowledge and engineering talent, macroeconomic governance that safeguards stability and manages risks, and continuous reform and opening-up.
Zhu said this process reflected "shengsheng," an idea from the ancient Chinese Book of Changes that emphasizes continuous renewal. "An economy is not a static set of indicators, but a living system that constantly sheds the old and brings forth the new," he told Xinhua.
Foreign-invested enterprises are also tapping into China's industrial upgrading. Their exports of high-tech products rose 42.1 percent in the first nine months, customs data showed.
Wang Jun, deputy head of the General Administration of Customs, said foreign firms were seizing opportunities arising from China's industrial upgrading and the development of new quality productive forces, while deepening their integration into the country's industrial and innovation chains.
Attention is now turning to how the momentum can carry through into the final quarter. Wei called for closer coordination of existing and additional policies, more effective investment in major projects and infrastructure, and wider use of new technologies to improve people's livelihoods.
"Steady economic performance also depends on a smooth transition between old and new growth drivers," Wei said. "The process will create more sources of growth and help ensure this year's economic and social development goals are achieved." ■

China Focus: China's top economic planner vows more efforts to expand domestic demand
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-20
20:15:48 CST
21:15:48 KST

BEIJING, Oct. 20 (Xinhua) -- China's top economic planner said Tuesday it will work with relevant departments to expand domestic demand with greater force and more effective measures in an effort to consolidate the foundation and momentum for steady economic recovery.
The National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) revealed this at a press conference on Tuesday following the release of the latest economic data on Monday, which showed the world's second-largest economy pressed ahead against pressures with a 4.6-percent economic growth in the first three quarters of 2026.
Commenting on the economic performance, NDRC official Zuo Gang said the economy, in the face of intensifying global geopolitical conflicts and frequent natural disasters, has demonstrated strong resilience and vitality with new growth drivers and improved structure.
Due to challenges such as the deepening impact of external shocks, an imbalance of strong supply and weak demand at home, and pronounced sectoral divergence, further measures will be taken to rev up the economy, according to the official.
"The NDRC will work with relevant departments to promptly introduce and implement incremental policies and promote synergy between existing and incremental policies with a view to achieving a good start for the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030)," Zuo said.
China has targeted 2026 growth at 4.5 to 5 percent and will strive for better in practice.
BOOSTING CONSUMPTION
More efforts will be made to vigorously boost consumption, Zuo said.
Authorities will raise the share of public service spending in fiscal expenditure, strengthen inclusive policies that reach consumers directly, and promote the expansion and upgrading of goods consumption, including new energy vehicles and smart products, Zuo said.
The push comes as consumption shows signs of steady improvement. Total retail sales of goods and services rose 2.6 percent year-on-year in the first three quarters of 2026, with retail sales of services growing faster than goods and new forms of consumption continuing to emerge, official data showed. Final consumption expenditure contributed more to overall economic growth in the January-September period.
Chinese authorities have recently introduced a raft of measures aimed at boosting domestic demand, including offering interest subsidies for the housing loans of eligible homebuyers to help reduce home-buying costs and better unlock housing demand.
Through ultra-long special treasury bond issuance, 250 billion yuan (about 37.2 billion U.S. dollars) has been raised to support consumer goods trade-in programs, and 200 billion yuan to support large-scale equipment upgrades this year. Furthermore, 50 billion yuan was earmarked for the establishment of a special fiscal-financial coordination fund to boost domestic demand.
In addition to measures already announced, including lowering interest rate for pledged supplementary lending and increasing relending quotas to support sci-tech innovation and technological upgrades, "we will introduce new incremental policies in a timely manner as needed to ensure that the economy operates within an appropriate range," Zuo said.
PROMOTING INVESTMENT
Zuo said China will invest in both physical assets and human capital to expand effective investment.
Specifically, the NDRC will push for the implementation of the 109 major projects outlined in the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) and the "six networks" initiative, covering water, power, computing, communications, urban underground pipelines and logistics networks, Zuo said.
Ultra-long special treasury bond funds will be deployed more effectively, and the new policy-based financial instruments will be used at a faster pace, Zuo said, also vowing stronger support for social welfare, technology innovation, industrial upgrading and security resilience.
Zuo revealed plans to energize private investment by introducing private capital into major nuclear power, hydropower, and water conservancy projects. He also identified the optimization of computing power facility layouts and the renovation and upgrading of aging reservoirs as additional investment priorities.
China's investment is undergoing a profound shift in emphasis from traditional sectors to emerging ones, analysts said, noting that artificial intelligence and new infrastructure will serve as key engines for the next round of effective investment.
Official data showed the country's investment in innovation-driven sectors held up well in the first three quarters of 2026, even as overall fixed-asset investment continued to contract. Investment in intellectual property products rose 9.3 percent year-on-year in the January-September period, while investment in high-tech industries grew 4.9 percent.
Investment will increasingly serve the development of new quality productive forces and the building of a modern industrial system, with the ultimate results felt in expanded employment, rising incomes and improved living standards, said Liu Yuanchun, president of Shanghai University of Finance and Economics. ■

Wetland reclamation brings limited crop gains, higher flood exposure: study
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-20
20:15:46 CST
21:15:46 KST

BEIJING, Oct. 20 (Xinhua) -- For years, converting wetlands into farmland has been seen as a practical way to grow more food. However, a new global study shows that this strategy may not be as beneficial as once thought and could carry greater risks than expected.
Researchers led by the Institute of Geographic Sciences and Natural Resources Research (IGSNRR) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, working with international partners, examined global croplands created from wetlands between 2000 and 2022. They assessed how much food these lands produced and their exposure to flooding. Their findings were recently published in the journal Nature Sustainability.
The findings show that wetland-reclaimed croplands contributed only marginally to global food production, accounting for just 0.1 percent of total crop output. In nearly half of these areas, yields were lower than on existing croplands, particularly for dryland crops. In 79 percent of the regions studied, their contribution to crop production was less than 1 percent.
These croplands also face significant flood exposure. Of these, 52 percent, covering about 21,000 square kilometers, are in areas prone to major flooding. On average, their flood exposure is 23 times that of croplands overall.
The study also found that 60 percent of wetland-reclaimed croplands combine limited agricultural benefits with high flood exposure. These areas are concentrated in East Asia, South Asia, North America, eastern South America and Oceania. They are especially common in food-importing or low-income countries.
According to Dong Jinwei, a researcher from IGSNRR, the study provides global evidence of the trade-offs between agricultural gains and ecological costs associated with wetland reclamation.
"Effective interventions are needed to ensure that agricultural expansion does not compromise critical wetland ecosystem services and long-term sustainability," Dong added. ■

From pregnancy to the first birthday — what payments can be received and how to apply
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-20
15:14:08 EEST

From pregnancy to the first birthday — what payments can be received and how to apply
Kyiv • UNN
Applications for assistance during pregnancy, childbirth, and childcare can be submitted through the Diia portal. Monthly payments amount to UAH 7 000.
In Ukraine, it is now possible to submit applications for financial assistance during pregnancy and childbirth and for childcare online. No trips to government institutions with a baby in your arms are necessary—you can apply for the payments in a few clicks on the Diia portal, reports UNN.
How much can be received:
-  UAH 7,000 — monthly pregnancy and childbirth assistance. Available to women who do not pay the SSC. The money is credited to an ordinary Diia.Card account and can be spent without restrictions.  To apply for the payment, a medical certificate confirming pregnancy and childbirth is required. 
-  UAH 7,000 (or UAH 10,500 for children with disabilities) — monthly childcare assistance for a child under one year old. These are earmarked funds credited to the special “Child Care” account. They may be spent exclusively on children’s needs: food, clothing, or care. Parents can also apply for the payments offline as before—at the Pension Fund, a CNAP, or through authorized representatives of territorial communities. 
How to apply:
-  Log in to the Diia portal and complete the first part of the application. The system will automatically verify your eligibility for the payments. 
-  If the verification is successful, a link to the second part of the application will be sent to your email. 
-  Complete and sign it with Diia.Signature within 24 hours. 
Both payments will be credited to a Diia.Card, but with different usage conditions. Pregnancy and childbirth assistance is paid without MCC-code restrictions. By contrast, the payment for the baby’s first year of life is earmarked. It is credited to the special “Child Care” account.

Women who meet the following criteria will be eligible for the assistance:
-  for childcare assistance—they have a child under one year and seven months old for whom they are not yet receiving assistance; 
-  for pregnancy and childbirth assistance—they still have a valid medical certificate of temporary incapacity or no more than six months have passed since it was closed; 
-  they are the child’s mother; 
-  they have a passport registered in the Unified State Demographic Register (USDR); 
-  they have a taxpayer registration number (TRN); 
-  they have a child under one year and seven months old for whom they are not yet receiving assistance; 
-  they have a registered place of residence or an actual place of residence if they have internally displaced person status.

A fugitive South Pacific Ponzi scammer—who later proclaimed himself “king” of a remote armed territory at the center of Papua New Guinea’s Bougainville island—has been given a royal burial following his death from an unspecified illness, according to local media and photographs of the funeral posted on social media.
Noah Musingku was accused of stealing tens of millions of dollars from victims across the region in a 1990s pyramid scheme known as U-Vistract. Following the collapse of the scheme, Musingku fled in the early 2000s to his home island of Bougainville, a region then still recovering from a devastating decade-long civil war.
Styling himself as King David Peii II of the twin kingdoms of Papaala and Me’ekamui, Musingku set up a pseudo-state with its own armed militia, banking system, and local currency known as the Bougainville kina (BVK). The BVK was later declared illegal by Papua New Guinea’s government.
A 2025 investigation by OCCRP revealed that, in the following decades, Musingku had built a global following among both locals and Western conspiracy theorists and adherents of “sovereign citizen” ideology. Followers of Musingku believed he would make them all wealthy and usher in a golden era of global peace and prosperity.
Still a fugitive until his death, Musingku survived an attack in 2006 by fighters aligned with Bougainville’s legally recognized government of former rebels. Four of Musingku’s bodyguards were killed in the attack, which left him with a bullet wound to the neck.
“He is indeed a man of great love for his fellow men and the world, full of compassion, humility, visionary leader, hard-working and sacrificial leader, and a great King that has shaken the foundations of nations and touched so many lives,” a death notice posted online attributed to the government of his self-declared kingdom said.
Photographs posted online show Musingku’s casket being carried and lowered into the ground in his “capital” of Tonu on Monday by an honor guard of camouflage-clad militia members while a small crowd of mourners looked on. Musingku’s grave was later covered with a mound of what appears to be sand and draped with an ornate cloth held down with large stones, as well as a flower bouquet.
Musingku’s death comes despite some followers believing he would reign for a thousand years. He was reportedly in his early 60s.

F1 Grand Prix in Austin: weekend schedule and the championship standings
Kyiv • UNN
The United States Grand Prix will take place in Austin on October 23–25. Antonelli leads Russell by 102 points and could clinch the title this Sunday.
From October 23 to 25, Austin, Texas, will host the 18th round of the 2026 Formula 1 season — the United States Grand Prix. This Sunday, at the Circuit of The Americas, championship leader Andrea Kimi Antonelli has a mathematical chance to secure his first title early, UNN reports.
United States Grand Prix weekend schedule in Austin
From Friday, October 23, to Sunday, October 25, the 18th round of the 2026 Formula 1 season — the United States Grand Prix — will take place at the Circuit of the Americas in Austin.
The sessions will take place as follows:
-  Friday, October 23: first practice: 20:30, second
practice: 00:00; 
-  Saturday, October 24: third practice: 20:30,
qualifying: 00:00. 
The race itself will take place on Sunday, October 25, at 22:00.
Features of the Circuit of the Americas
The Circuit of The Americas (COTA), designed by Hermann Tilke in cooperation with the American architectural firm HKS, had a somewhat troubled start, as several setbacks occurred during construction. However, the wait proved worthwhile when 1978 Formula 1 champion Mario Andretti officially opened the circuit on October 21, 2012.
In 2012, the Circuit of The Americas hosted a Formula 1 race for the first time — it was the first United States Grand Prix since the 2007 race in Indianapolis. As expected, more than 100,000 spectators filled the grandstands in Austin to witness Lewis Hamilton's final victory for McLaren before his move to Mercedes in 2013.
The United States Grand Prix begins with a 250-meter stretch from pole position to the braking point before Turn 1 — an uphill corner that is wide enough to give drivers the opportunity to choose their line and allow the competitors to regroup before the completion of the first lap.
The first Formula 1 race at the Circuit of The Americas took place in 2012 — it was the first United States Grand Prix since 2007. Since then, the race has attracted one of the largest audiences in the sport, while Lewis Hamilton became world champion here in both 2015 and 2019.
Here is what makes this circuit such an exciting challenge and why this event attracts so many spectators.
The championship standings before the round
Kimi Antonelli has remained at the top of the drivers' standings since the third round of the season in Japan — and his lead grew even stronger after he finished on the podium at the most recent Singapore Grand Prix.
After the 17th round of the season, the Italian leads his closest pursuer, George Russell, by 102 points, while Lewis Hamilton, who is in third place, trails by 111 points.
Mathematically, five other drivers remain in the title fight alongside Antonelli — Russell, Hamilton, Max Verstappen, Charles Leclerc and Lando Norris.
However, the real chances of those lower down the standings winning the title are negligible, as their chances of victory depend on Antonelli not scoring more points and no other driver exceeding the Italian's current tally of 340 points.
Under this scenario, Russell, Hamilton and Verstappen would have to wait until the round in Qatar to win the title, while Leclerc and Norris could win it only in Abu Dhabi.
To win the championship, Antonelli must win, while Russell must finish ninth or lower. Hamilton must also cross the finish line fifth or lower, while Verstappen can finish in any position.
In other words, to secure his first world championship title in Austin, Antonelli needs to score 23 more points than Russell, 14 more than Hamilton and six more than Verstappen.
Recall
Red Bull driver Max Verstappen secured pole position for the sprint at the 2026 Singapore Grand Prix. Despite a dramatic incident involving a possible rules violation under yellow flags, the stewards decided not to penalize the Dutch driver.

Marseille braces for more unrest after protests give way to 'apocalyptic' disorder
- Published
Thunder and lightning have boomed across Marseille following the weekend's mayhem, illuminating the cracked windows and boarded-up doors of hundreds of businesses that were smashed as protests gave way to disorder.
France's second city saw some of the worst violence as chaos gripped the country on Saturday. Local business leaders say more than 500 premises were damaged, and the majority looted.
A police union boss told the BBC that the weekend had been an "apocalyptic" hell for his colleagues. 118 officers were injured, representing more than a tenth of the national figure.
So far, 101 arrests have been made in the port city, a quarter of them children.
But by Monday, it was police who were most conspicuous on the city's streets, not protesters. For eight hours, demonstrations and gatherings were banned in an effort to avoid a third consecutive day of disorder.
- Suspect arrested after historic town hall set alight - French media 
  - Published14 hours ago
It seemed to work; the largest central gathering we witnessed was a posse of weather-beaten tourists trudging around the quayside.
Nonetheless, an overnight curfew for minors will come into force in parts of the city from Tuesday evening. An overnight curfew in parts of Paris, which came into force on Monday, has also been extended.
Marseille is one of France's most ethnically diverse cities – a place where generations of new arrivals have landed.
18-year-old student Maryame only arrived in the southern city a few weeks ago, albeit from the countryside not too far away.
"It was very scary because it's my first time in a big city, and also my first time demonstrating," she said.
Maryame said violence engulfed the student demonstration her friends had joined as looters began attacking shops.
She said the solidarity of the earlier march was "beautiful" and the subsequent disorder "terrifying", but went on to say that she was conflicted as to whether even more violence would make the government sit up and listen.
"It is a very complicated question if violence is legitimate," she began.
"But the thing is, France, our history is really based on revolution, and sometimes we really have to make a really big impact.
"Sometimes it goes too far."
'An unheard-of level of violence'
For the police, the extent to which order disintegrated was a shock, according to one organisation representing rank and file officers.
"It was a war," said Arnaud Blaise from the UN1TE police union. "An unheard-of level of violence. Unprecedented."
Looting was reported across the city centre, including along La Canebière - Marseille's equivalent of Paris's Champs-Élysées - Rue Paradis, and at the Centre Bourse shopping centre. Businesses were also hit further afield, such as in the Grand Littoral and Le Merlan shopping malls to the north.
Blaise said he was concerned that future protests could follow the same destructive pattern as Saturday, with young people from the deprived northern suburbs seizing the opportunity to steal amid chaos that, in his view, was stirred up by far-left agitators - referred to in France as the Black Bloc.
"The Black Blocs provoked, and the youngsters took advantage to start looting," Blaise said. "That created chaos, with police officers running right, running left, and in effect, we got overwhelmed."
I put it to Blaise that the police had been accused of heavy-handedness with peaceful students but sitting back as the most violent protesters pillaged local businesses.
"That is not the case at all," he replied, arguing that more police than students had been injured.
"Four thousand tear gas grenades were fired and then we ran out of ammunition. So at a certain point, you have no choice but to retreat."

  - Published2 days ago
France's Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez - whose resignation in the wake of the riots was rejected by President Macron - travelled to Marseille on Monday evening.
He came to the City Hall, which was briefly occupied by protestors on Saturday, and met Marseille's Socialist Mayor Benoît Payan.
Payan said he wanted answers from the government as to how the chaos was allowed to happen.
"Order was lost, and an attempt was made to restore order. I believe that from start to finish, it was a fiasco," he said on Monday.
He said under-staffed and poorly deployed police needed to change their tactics.
"If there isn't a radical change of approach on this issue - if, by chance, the only target remains high school students - then we will see looting scenes again."
He continued: "I don't know what's left to loot in Marseille, but for the little that remains, it will be looted."
While the ban on public gatherings in Marseille and partial overnight curfews in other French cities have brought some temporary calm, more demonstrations are planned for the weekend.
At a smashed out tram stop, 79-year-old grandmother Chantal Bellanger said she had been "worried - but then, I've been worried for a long time".
"We can clearly see that France has lost its grip on many things. Public services, hospitals, education is in a horrible state, the peripheral neighbourhoods are dilapidated, they are abandoned."
She said she used to work in these deprived northern suburbs, where poverty and crime rates are very high, and feared a whole lost generation was criminalising itself through anger and despair.
"It tugs at your heartstrings," she said.
"To see children whose actions are going to place them completely outside of society. It's painful to watch."

====================================================================================================

The unravelling alliance – when Israel’s interests clash with America’s
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-20
12:08:00 UTC
21:08:00 KST

The relationship between the United States and Israel has long been presented as an alliance founded on shared democratic values, strategic interests and an enduring commitment to regional security. But beneath this familiar narrative, a more difficult question is emerging: what happens when an ally’s regional ambitions begin to undermine the wider interests of the superpower that sustains it?
The United States is a global power with responsibilities extending far beyond Israel. It must protect maritime trade, maintain energy security, manage relations with major powers, reassure its regional partners and prevent conflicts from spiralling into wider wars. Israel, meanwhile, has increasingly pursued a security doctrine centred on military dominance, pre-emptive action and the persistent neutralisation of perceived threats. These objectives may overlap, but they are not identical. When they diverge, the alliance faces a test that personal ties between political leaders cannot indefinitely postpone.
The price of unconditional support
American support for Israel has provided diplomatic protection, military assistance and formidable strategic advantages. Yet support without meaningful conditions carries its own costs.
When Washington is seen as endorsing Israeli military actions regardless of their consequences, it risks surrendering the moral authority it invokes in defence of international law, civilian protection and a rules-based international order.
This is not simply a question of public relations. It affects America’s credibility with countries whose cooperation it needs elsewhere. A superpower cannot convincingly demand restraint from adversaries while appearing unwilling to exercise comparable influence over its closest allies. Nor can it expect the world to distinguish indefinitely between American declarations of principle and the consequences of American policy.
The damage is increasingly visible in public opinion. A Pew Research Center survey published in April 2026 found that 60 per cent of American adults held an unfavourable view of Israel, compared with 53 per cent a year earlier. Negative views have grown across political constituencies, particularly among younger Americans. These figures do not mean that American support for Israel has disappeared, but they do suggest that the political foundations of the relationship are changing. (Pew Research Center)
A relationship that once enjoyed broad political protection is becoming more contested. For Israel, this should be a warning. For Washington, it should prompt a serious reassessment of whether an alliance is being managed in a way that serves American interests or increasingly constrains American choices.
Iran: The test of strategic independence
Iran illustrates the growing danger of divergent priorities. Washington must consider not only Iran’s military capabilities and regional relationships, but also the consequences of prolonged confrontation for shipping, energy prices, American forces and the stability of neighbouring states. Israel’s leadership, by contrast, may regard continued military pressure as indispensable to preventing Iran from rebuilding its capabilities and influence.
The difference is fundamental. A military operation can weaken an adversary without resolving the political conditions that sustain the conflict. It can also provoke retaliation, widen the theatre of war and impose costs on countries that neither initiated the confrontation nor wish to become participants in it.
The question is not whether Washington and Tel Aviv should have identical assessments of Iran. Allies will inevitably differ. The real question is whether Israel expects the United States to underwrite an open-ended confrontation even when Washington concludes that the strategic, economic and human costs outweigh the likely gains.
If Israel refuses to budge on key questions, it may discover that American support has limits. The United States could eventually decide that containing a conflict, securing maritime routes and preserving regional stability matter more than accommodating every Israeli demand. That would not necessarily mean abandoning Israel; it would mean asserting that an alliance cannot confer an unlimited right to determine another country’s foreign policy.
India cannot replace America
Israel’s search for a wider network of strategic partners is understandable. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has reportedly advocated diversifying partnerships, including closer relations with India and countries in Latin America, partly in anticipation of a less supportive future American administration. (Times of India)
India and Israel have developed significant cooperation in defence, technology, agriculture and intelligence. Their relationship is important to both countries. But it would be a mistake to assume that India can simply step into the role occupied by the United States. American military assistance, diplomatic influence, intelligence capabilities and global reach operate on a scale that no single emerging partner can readily reproduce.
India also has its own national interests. It must balance relations across West Asia, protect its energy supplies, safeguard its large expatriate community in the Gulf and maintain diplomatic space with countries that have sharply different positions on Israel and Iran. Its foreign policy cannot be reduced to an extension of Israeli strategic priorities.
The same caution applies to Latin America. New partnerships may widen Israel’s diplomatic options, but they cannot automatically reproduce Washington’s influence or insulate Israel from the consequences of regional escalation.
The Gulf is hedging—and so are its neighbours
The Gulf states have their own reasons to question a strategy that leaves the region vulnerable to repeated military crises. They must protect energy infrastructure, trade routes, investment, economic diversification and domestic stability. Even where governments share concerns about Iran, that does not mean they welcome every Israeli or American decision that risks triggering retaliation.
Jordan and Egypt face their own calculations. Both have enduring security relationships with Washington and established peace agreements with Israel, but neither can ignore the domestic and regional consequences of a conflict that intensifies popular anger or threatens regional stability. Their cooperation cannot simply be presumed to amount to unconditional endorsement of Israeli policy.
Recent developments underline the complexity of these calculations. Egypt’s reported consideration of possible military support for Saudi Arabia amid escalating regional tensions demonstrates how governments may adjust their positions in response to immediate security and economic pressures. It should not be mistaken for a simple alignment behind Israel or Washington. (Reuters, 19 October 2026)
This is the strategic reality Israel must confront: regional governments can cooperate with it on particular issues while resisting its wider ambitions. They can depend on American security guarantees while seeking to avoid becoming hostages to American or Israeli decisions. Hedging is not necessarily hostility; it is a rational response to uncertainty.
An alliance cannot survive on history alone
The United States and Israel remain closely connected, and neither has an easy substitute for the relationship. But history, shared interests and established military cooperation cannot eliminate the need for strategic accountability. Washington must ask whether its support strengthens regional security or enables policies that repeatedly place that security at risk. Israel, in turn, must recognise that the power of an ally cannot be treated as a permanent resource available without regard to the ally’s wider interests.
There is a danger that Israel’s pursuit of security through ever-expanding military pressure will produce the opposite result: greater regional uncertainty, deeper diplomatic isolation and a growing reluctance among partners to identify themselves too closely with its actions. A state can possess formidable military capabilities and still lose political room to manoeuvre.
For Washington, the choice is equally consequential. Uncritical support may preserve short-term cooperation, but it can weaken American moral standing, strain relations with other partners and reduce the credibility of its diplomacy.
A superpower that cannot distinguish between an ally’s national interests and its own global responsibilities risks allowing the former to dictate the latter.
The central question is no longer whether the United States and Israel are allies. It is whether their alliance can adapt to the limits of shared interests. If Israel refuses to recognise those limits, it may find that the search for alternative partners offers less protection than it imagines. And if Washington refuses to exercise independent judgement, it may discover that loyalty to an ally has come at the expense of its own strategic freedom and international credibility.
Ultimately, the greatest danger for Israel may not be the loss of American assistance alone, but the gradual erosion of the political understanding that has made such assistance possible. No country, however strategically important, can indefinitely expect a superpower to absorb the diplomatic damage, economic disruption and moral consequences of decisions over which it has diminishing influence. Nor can Israel assume that regional states will continue to accommodate its security demands while their own populations, economies and national interests bear the costs of permanent confrontation. The United States must recover the independence to say no when an ally’s actions threaten wider peace, just as Israel must recognise that security cannot be built on the perpetual insecurity of its neighbours. An alliance is not a blank cheque, and friendship between nations cannot mean the surrender of judgement.
If Washington fails to draw that distinction, it will weaken itself to protect Israel; if Israel refuses to understand it, it may discover that the very alliance on which it has depended is no longer willing to follow where it leads.
